topic.name: Solving Rational Equations Containing Binomials Using Cross-Multiplication

question.explanation:
First, note that $x = \dfrac{1}{2}$ and $x = -\dfrac{1}{3}$ cannot be solutions since division by $0$ is undefined.

To solve the equation, we first apply cross-multiplication:

\begin{align*} \dfrac{9}{6x - 3} & = \dfrac{2}{3x + 1}\\[5pt] 9 \cdot (3x + 1) & = (6x - 3) \cdot 2\\[5pt] 27x + 9 & = 12x - 6 \end{align*}

Then, we apply the addition and multiplication principles, as usual: \begin{align*} 27x + 9 & = 12x - 6\\[5pt] 27x + 9 -12x & = 12x - 6 -12x\\[5pt] 15x + 9 & = -6\\[5pt] 15x + 9 - 9& = -6 - 9\\[5pt] 15x & = -15\\[5pt] \dfrac{15x}{15} & =\dfrac{-15}{15}\\[5pt] x & = -1 \end{align*}

Since $x = -1$ is different from $x = \dfrac{1}{2}$ and $x = -\dfrac{1}{3},$ we can accept it as a solution. Thus, the solution is $x = -1.$

example.title: Solving Rational Equations Containing Binomials in Both Denominators

question.explanation:
First, note that $x=-4$ cannot be a solution since division by $0$ is undefined.

To solve the equation, we first apply cross-multiplication:

\[ \eqalign{ \dfrac{2}{3x+12} &= \dfrac{2}{x+4} \\[5pt] 2 \cdot (x+4) &= (3x+12) \cdot 2 \\[5pt] 2x + 8 &= 6x + 24 } \]

Then, we apply the addition and multiplication principles, as usual:

\[ \eqalign{ 2x + 8 &= 6x + 24 \\[5pt] 2x + 8-24 &= 6x + 24-24 \\[5pt] 2x-16 &= 6x \\[5pt] 2x-16-2x &= 6x-2x \\[5pt] -16 &= 4x \\[5pt] \dfrac{-16}{4} &= \dfrac{4x}{4} \\[5pt] -4 &= x } \]

Since $x=-4$ cannot be a solution, the equation has no solutions.

example.title: Solving Rational Equations Containing Binomials in Both Denominators

question.explanation:
First, note that $x=-3 $ and $x=1$ cannot be solutions since division by $0$ is undefined.

To solve the equation, we first apply cross-multiplication: \begin{align} \dfrac{1}{x-1} & = \dfrac{2}{x+3} \\[5pt] 1 \cdot (x+3) & = (x-1) \cdot 2\\[5pt] x+3 & = 2x-2 \end{align}

Then, we apply the addition and multiplication principles, as usual: \begin{align} x+3 & = 2x-2 \\[5pt] x+3-x & = 2x-2-x \\[5pt] 3 & = x-2\\[5pt] 3+2 & = x-2+2\\[5pt] 5 & = x \end{align}

Since $x = 5$ is different from $x=-3$ and $x=1,$ we can accept it as a solution. Thus, the solution is $x=5.$
